name: TESSERA NeuroVeil NV-2 Interface Disruptor
description:
The TESSERA NV-2 NeuroVeil is a topical neurotransmitter-interference compound delivered in a fine mist aerosol designed to penetrate the dermal interface zones of standard BCI hardware. Brain-computer interfaces rely on transdermal contact pads, induction coils, and micro-port arrays that necessarily expose small areas of biological tissue to the external environment — and it is precisely these interface zones that the NV-2 targets. The active compound is a synthetic glycoprotein analogue designated TX-119, developed from TESSERA's own BCI research division. When TX-119 contacts exposed BCI interface tissue, it binds to the glycocalyx layer of the interface neurons and temporarily disrupts the electrochemical signaling that allows the BCI to read and write neural data. The result is a cascade of degraded BCI function: visual overlays fragment, audio implants produce static or dropout, motor-assist augmentations lose calibration, and in some cases the subject experiences involuntary sensory hallucinations generated by corrupted feedback loops.

The NV-2 is a legitimate TESSERA product, sold through licensed security channels as a 'BCI-interference compliance tool' for use by certified security professionals dealing with subjects whose augmentations pose a tactical threat. Its legal status reflects a careful corporate calculation: TESSERA profits both from selling BCI systems and from selling tools that can disable competitors' BCI systems in security contexts. The compound is agent-specific — it does not affect biological tissue beyond minor transient irritation at the contact site — but the BCI disruption effects can be severe enough to cause falls, disorientation, and inability to use augmentation-dependent motor functions for 8–20 minutes depending on interface density.

Civil liberties organizations have repeatedly challenged the NV-2's licensed status, arguing that deliberately disrupting a person's neurological augmentation — which may include sensory prosthetics, communication systems, or medical monitoring hardware — constitutes a form of assault qualitatively distinct from conventional incapacitating sprays. TESSERA has successfully lobbied to maintain the licensed classification in all five GLMZ administrative zones.
legality: Licensed — requires certified security professional credential; use against medical BCI hardware is specifically prohibited under GLMZ Augmentation Protection Statute 44.7, though enforcement is inconsistent
specifications:
Active compound: TX-119 glycoprotein analogue (2.8% concentration)
Delivery: fine-mist aerosol, 2-micron particle size
Target tissue: BCI dermal interface zones, transdermal induction sites
Primary effect: BCI signal disruption, overlay fragmentation, motor-assist decalibration
Secondary effect: transient skin irritation at contact site
Duration of effect: 8–20 minutes (varies by interface density)
Effective range: 0.5–2m
Net volume: 60ml
Price: Φ620
tactical_use: Used by corporate security teams to neutralize subjects whose BCI augmentations provide tactical advantages — targeting reticles, encrypted communications, enhanced reflexes routed through neural interfaces, or drone control links. Application to the face, neck, and wrist interface zones produces the fastest effect. Security doctrine for NV-2 deployment typically includes immediate physical restraint following application, as the disruption window is finite and a recovering subject may become more dangerous as their augmentations come back online.
cultural_context: In augmented communities, the NV-2 is regarded with particular hostility — being 'ghostmade' (hit with neural fog) is described as a deeply disorienting and frightening experience, as subjects lose access to perceptions and capabilities they may have depended on for years. Some heavily augmented individuals describe the sensation as akin to sudden partial blindness. Street resellers who obtain NV-2 canisters charge significant premiums. The spray has a quiet but growing presence in organized crime, used to neutralize augmented security personnel or rival operators before a takedown.
known_users: licensed private security firms handling augmented subjects
story_hooks: A TESSERA-employed fixer is found dead — not shot, but fallen from a height, with NV-2 residue on their interface ports, suggesting their motor-assist augmentation failed mid-operation. The NV-2 canister used is a TESSERA production batch that was supposedly never distributed.

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact, clinical aerosol dispenser with a minimalist design that reads as medical-grade rather than weaponized. The form factor resembles a high-end inhaler or precision spray applicator — ergonomic, refined, almost pharmacy-counter legitimate. The silhouette is tapered and purposeful, designed for one-handed deployment with thumb-actuated trigger.
physical_description.dimensions: 12cm height × 4.2cm width × 3.8cm depth. Valve stem protrudes 0.8cm from cap. Pressurized chamber comprises roughly 60% of total volume.
physical_description.weight_description: Surprisingly light — barely 140 grams when full. The heft is concentrated in the lower third (pressurized chamber), creating a bottom-heavy balance that feels stable and controlled in the palm. Feels like holding a precision tool rather than a weapon.
physical_description.primary_material: Anodized aluminum body with surgical-grade stainless steel valve assembly and pressurized chamber. Polymer actuator trigger and thumb-rest. Internal delivery lines are medical-grade silicone.
physical_description.finish: Matte silver-gray anodization with a brushed texture that resists fingerprints and reflects light evenly. The aluminum has a clinical, almost sterile appearance — no visible wear marks on new units, though used examples show faint handling marks on the grip area.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: matte gunmetal gray. Accents: stainless steel valve cap (polished), minimalist black safety band around trigger guard, subtle electric-blue indicator dot on the pressure gauge window (glows faintly under UV).
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer grip surface with micro-ridges for tactile control, slightly tacky to discourage slipping when wet. The feel is clinical and precise — designed for security professional hands wearing nitrile or latex gloves.
distinctive_features: Transparent polycarbonate pressure gauge window with blue-tinted gradient readout showing remaining volume and pressure status
Fine-mist actuator nozzle (adjustable between 0.5m tight spray and 2m diffuse cloud) with secondary precision tip attachment
CLARITY MEDITATION corporate seal embossed on the lower chamber (small, understated)
TX-119 concentration and batch date printed in white on the spine in corporate sans-serif font
Safety interlock trigger guard prevents accidental discharge
Integrated locking cap that doubles as a pressure release valve
Faint residue marks on professional-used units — microscopic whitish deposits near the nozzle from TX-119 compound settling
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: CLARITY MEDITATION logo (geometric tessellation pattern) discreetly embossed on the chamber side. Serial number and compliance stamps (GLMZ 44.7, licensed security only) printed in small white text on the upper spine. Batch/manufacturing date etched into the metal near the base.
physical_description.condition_typical: Fresh units appear pristine and clinical — almost pharmacy-counter legitimate. Field-used examples show minimal wear: slight grip polish, microscopic scratches from holster contact, occasional faint crystalline deposits near the nozzle from compound exposure. Well-maintained professional gear; rarely shows heavy battle damage because the NV-2 is not designed for combat durability but for precision application.
